title: Murmuration — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Murmuration's rich face, its first round at Study tier and still a proposal: three made pieces that put the page's claims to the page's own flock (the one plane and its Cohesion knob, the Disorder knee tried as a phase transition, the blind pair put to the reader's ear), with the steward's renders, plots, 3D view and instrument gathered beside the sentences they answer. I grow when Loudon has heard them; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.section: The phase transition as the signature macro
offers.what: 'Snap' and 'second-order', measured on the page's flock at 30 to 240 birds: the turn is a real phase transition by three marks (the wobble peaks at the knee at every size; the peak grows 1.01 to 2.65 and the 90-to-10% drop narrows from η 0.097 to 0.066 as the flock grows; no memory at 60 and 120 birds). But it is a steep knee, not a jump, and at 240 birds the way up stays more ordered at η 0.06 by 0.124 (four standard errors). Offer: 'the steep knee of a real transition' for 'snap', and 'second-order' held as what the flock does at the instrument's sizes, 8 to 120 birds (Grégoire and Chaté 2004 found the Vicsek transition turns discontinuous in large flocks, a finding that was disputed).

offers.section: The phase transition as the signature macro
offers.what: The remapped slider (η = 0.25·x²) spreads the 90-to-10% drop over 36% of the travel; on the first build's linear knob it took 9%. So the knee is about four times gentler under the hand than when the section was written, though still far from a crossfade (80%). Whether that is still the snap the forward vector asks to keep ('not soften into a crossfade') is Loudon's call; the page could say which slider it means.

offers.section: The phase transition as the signature macro
offers.what: 'The flock crystallizes from broadband noise into a coherent tone' comes true only under the order mapping (heading is pitch). Under the first build's mapping, the one the Architecture section describes, the sound's pitch focus did not follow the flock (3.38 to 3.46 bits of pitch-class entropy throughout; page-as-built.wav). Under the order mapping it narrows to 2.45 to 2.67 bits when ordered: a tightened cluster, not one tone (0 bits). Steward's measurement, cycle 1; offer: name the mapping that carries the transition to the ear, and 'toward a tone' for 'into a coherent tone'.

offers.section: The phase transition as the signature macro
offers.what: The headless numbers hold on re-run (φ 0.099 to past 0.9 in 5.7 s at η 0, seed 7; 0.114 at η 0.80, the floor √(π/240) = 0.114), but η 0.80 is now beyond the instrument's Disorder slider, which tops out at η 0.25 (φ already 0.13 there). Offer: note the slider's range beside the numbers, and 'past 0.9' or the measured 0.96 at 60 s for '0.93'.

offers.section: The Architecture — one plane, three readings
offers.what: Cohesion's morph holds only over the top of the knob. Measured on the page's flock (η 0.06, four starts): up to 1.25 the flock spreads nearly as wide as random (254 to 286 px against 305; pitches 5.3 to 5.5 semitones against 5.5); it gathers between 1.5 and 2, often into a few clumps (a chord more than a tone); it reaches one tone only near 3 (41 px, 1.1 semitones). The instrument's default, 1.0, sits on the cloud end. Offer: say where on the knob the morph lives, or move the default.

offers.section: The Architecture — one plane, three readings
offers.what: The grains reading as described (screen-height sets pitch, speed drives grain density, 'This is the reading the prototype builds') is the first build's mapping. Since 2026-10-14 the instrument's default is the order mapping (heading is pitch, one octave around; grain length follows how steady a bird's course is), and all three readings are built, as the Open Decisions answer already says. Offer: describe both mappings, and drop 'the reading the prototype builds'.

The blind verdict is in: Loudon answered 'can't tell' on 2026-10-15 (murmuration-steward-003), and the key is open in engine/blind-key.json. The line '— progressed: … the verdict is Loudon's, waiting on the board' is out of date (the steward proposes the same, item 2 of its tuning). Measured on the takes: the flock's pitch is more focused in the ordered stretch (2.45 against 2.88 bits) and the scare (2.96 against 3.24), the same elsewhere; the steward's reading is that coordination alone isn't audible at this mapping.

pieces.title: four moments in 3D · steward, cycle 4
pieces.caption: The flock over its wavetable, from the steward's 3D view on the same engine as the renders. The ground is the terrain; a bird's altitude is how steady its course has been, the number that sets its grain length. Melted (φ 0.17), the birds skim low and click; ordering (φ 0.70), they lift as one sheet; a strike tears the sheet (35 birds alarmed); and the pad's pillars turn one hue as the chord collapses to one pitch class. Stills from headless Chrome.

verdicts.why: Shows 'one plane' at a glance; φ 0.17 and 0.70 match three-d/3d-report.json (0.165, 0.699).

sections.heading: The Architecture — one plane, three readings

pieces.by: the Maker · the page's flock and grain voice, live
pieces.title: One plane · four steps
pieces.caption: **The plane built up, and the Cohesion claim tried.** Four steps: the terrain of four corner waveforms, with the point under your finger as a steady tone; one bird as a grain voice under the section's own mapping (place is timbre, height is pitch, speed is grain rate); sixty birds as a cloud, their pitches counted; then Cohesion over the instrument's whole range, 0 to 3. Measured on the page's flock, equal to the engine, four starts a setting: cohesion does gather the flock into one tone at the top of the knob (at 3, a spread of 41 px and pitches within 1.1 semitones), but only there. Up to 1.25 the flock spreads nearly as wide as birds dropped at random (254 to 286 px against 305); it gathers between 1.5 and 2, often into a few clumps; the instrument's default, 1.0, sits on the cloud end. Pitch spread measures focus, not how broadband the sound is; heard by no ear.

pieces.caption: **All three readings from one engine, playable.** The steward's 3D view pastes the engine in unchanged: grains by default, the density pad as a field of pillars, and a click that sends a startle through the flock. pieces.title: one click, four answers · steward, cycle 3
pieces.caption: Four identical clicks land in four different flocks. A settled flock hit at the centre loses order from 0.94 to 0.54 and is back in 4.2 s; the same click upper left shatters it to 0.13; a third, into the broken flock, alarms only 5 birds. An authored envelope would give four copies.

pieces.caption: Where the startle swell stands clearest, at 3 s and 10 s: +3.3 and +5.6 dB over a no-click floor of 1.9 dB.

verdicts.why: A real test that pushes back: cohesion is flat to 1.25 and gathers only at 1.5–3, and my sweep at η 0, 0.03 and 0.06 shows that holds off the knee too. Note: at η 0 and 0.03 the tightest setting is 2.5, not 3, so 'one tone near 3' is true at the default η only.
All three readings from one engine, playable; the caption is honest that nobody has heard it in the face.
Gives the pad's sentence a sound; the caption points the ear at the right seconds.
The nearest thing on the page to a test of 'an organic swell no envelope produces'; 0.94→0.54 in 4.17 s, 0.13, 5 birds all match engine/gesture_analysis.json.
+3.3 and +5.6 dB over a 1.9 dB floor match the place strikes A and B.

sections.heading: The phase transition as the signature macro

pieces.by: the Maker · the page's flock and grain voice, live
pieces.title: The knee · four steps
pieces.caption: **Snap, or a curved knob?** The page's own flock, equal to the engine to the last digit over 1200 frames, heard through its own grain voice and walked up: one bird turning toward its neighbours against the Disorder knob, then sixty birds and their one number φ, then the slider swept against a crossfade, then the test. Measured here: on the instrument's slider the flock gives up its order, 90% of the way to 10%, over 36% of the travel (a crossfade: 80%; the first build's linear knob: 9%). The wobble, N times the variance of φ, peaks at η 0.06 to 0.07, where φ is halfway down, at every size from 30 to 240 birds; growing the flock at the same crowding raises that peak from 1.01 to 2.65 and narrows the drop from η 0.097 to 0.066. Those are the marks of a real phase transition, which a curved knob doesn't leave. It comes back the way it went at 60 and 120 birds; at 240 the way up stays more ordered at η 0.06, by 0.124 (four standard errors), which this sweep can't tell from slow settling. The section's own numbers hold: at η 0 φ goes from 0.10 past 0.9 in 5.7 s; at η 0.80 it sits at 0.114, the floor for sixty random birds. Checked by the check beside it; heard by no ear.

pieces.title: the knee, and the first mapping that missed it · steward, cycle 1
pieces.caption: Top: φ against η, eight starts, with slow sweeps up and down; on the first build's linear slider the whole transition sat in its first sixth. Bottom: a 40-second performance where the flock orders and melts. Under the first mapping (height is pitch) the sound's pitch focus hardly moves; under the order mapping (heading is pitch) it follows the flock.
pieces.near: Headless verification of the prototype model

pieces.title: the first build, ordering and melting · 40 s
pieces.caption: The same performance through the mapping as first built: the flock crystallises and melts, and the sound barely changes (pitch-class entropy 3.38 to 3.46 bits throughout). The section's "crystallizes from broadband noise into a coherent tone" needed the order mapping to come true.
pieces.near: the flock crystallizes from broadband noise

verdicts.why: Wording only, in check.mjs summarise() then --build: the 240-bird memory does not hold (new seeds 0.088 at 2.5 se; 60 s settling gives −0.004; a −2.56 se gap of the other sign sits at η 0.11), so say no memory is established; and Grégoire–Chaté was 'disputed for this angular noise, and answered' (Chaté et al. 2008), not just 'disputed'.
Evidence, honestly captioned; 'first sixth' of the old linear slider matches Murmuration.html:464-466.
Makes offer 3 heard: the flock orders and the sound doesn't follow (3.38–3.46 bits, engine/takes_analysis.json).

pieces.title: the instrument · p5.js and an AudioWorklet
pieces.caption: **The instrument itself.** Press Engage, then play: Disorder is the phase-transition macro (η = 0.25·x², the knee at mid-slider), Listen by chooses the reading (order, place or density), a click drops the predator and a drag pulls the flock. It carries its own review layer. Proven equal to the engine on 1200 frames; heard in a browser by no agent.

verdicts.why: The instrument, proven equal to the engine (check_page_mapping.js: 0). Note: 'knee at mid-slider' is true at 60 birds; at 120 in the same field the middle moves to about η 0.085, x 0.58.

pieces.title: the ceiling climb in headless Chrome · steward, cycle 5
pieces.caption: The ceiling test after a full climb, 60 birds to 720, one strike a step: clean through 360, 420 right on the line (59% of the audio thread), strained from 480, over at 720 (101%, 858 dropouts). Headless Chrome on an M1 Max; Firefox and Safari still unmeasured.

verdicts.why: Matches ceiling-headless-chrome.json; the report reads 420 as clean (cleanUpTo 420), so 'right on the line' is the stricter reading, which is fine.

pieces.by: the Maker · the steward's blind takes
pieces.title: The blind pair · four steps
pieces.caption: **The wager, put to your ear.** The steward's two 40-second takes of one performance: one the flock, one a cloud handed the flock's centre, spread, speed, heading agreement and grain-length mix every frame, with only who-steers-by-whom left out. The piece walks up from the score both takes follow, through what a hand can copy, to the two on one switch, and only then asks which is alive. The key, Loudon's own answer and a measurement of the two open after you answer, not before.

verdicts.why: The walk-up unblinds it: step 2, 'the other take … the hard version of a hand-dialed cloud', plays take Y, and Y is the copy (blind-key.json). Play one take and the other with neither named, explain the copy away from any take, or shuffle A/B per visit and let the key name both.
